title: Rafael and the Vector
premise: Dominic Reyes, a clone decanted from a murdered investigator's memories, arrives at the dying colony of Vector to close a case the original never solved. As she records the colony's slow abandonment, she finds her predecessor's name erased from the manifest of a ship that officially never flew—and discovers the original was killed to bury evidence that Earth's last transmission loop is a fabrication keeping two fleets from war. Falling for Rafael, a colony archivist who knew the original and sees through her, Dominic must choose between exposing the truth and preserving the lie that holds the peace. In the end, she broadcasts the case under both their names, accepting exile so the fleets stay apart and the forgotten colony is finally remembered.
about_author: Silas Okafor is a former orbital logistics auditor who turned to fiction after a decade spent reconciling manifests that refused to match. He writes from a converted cargo module in Lagos, where he collects dead satellites' final transmissions.

chapters.title: Decant
chapters.summary: Dominic wakes aboard the transport with her original's memories still settling, reviewing the unsolved murder file on approach to Vector. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: disorientation and the uncanny grief of inheriting a stranger's life—and his enemies.

chapters.title: The Colony That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Dominic surveys Vector's half-empty habitats and meets Rafael, the archivist cataloguing everything before the power fails. He recognizes her face but says nothing. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath bureaucratic routine.

chapters.title: Manifest of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing shipping records, Dominic finds the original's name scrubbed from the Meridian's manifest—a ship logged as never having launched. Rafael admits he helped falsify it. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: first betrayal of trust, first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: What Rafael Kept
chapters.summary: Rafael shows her the original's hidden recordings: proof the transmission loop from Earth is a decades-old recording maintained by both fleets' leadership. POV: alternating Dominic and Rafael. Emotional beat: intimacy born of shared complicity.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Silence
chapters.summary: Dominic reconstructs the political architecture: two rival fleets orbiting Earth, kept apart only by belief in a living homeworld. The original died trying to prove otherwise. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited duty.

chapters.title: The Loop Ends
chapters.summary: The transmission loop degrades ahead of schedule; fleet sensors begin pinging Vector for answers. A fleet envoy arrives demanding Dominic certify the colony as operational fiction. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: pressure tightening; invisibility failing.

chapters.title: Certify
chapters.summary: Under orders, Dominic signs the false certification—her first act as her own person is a lie. Rafael, disgusted, stops speaking to her. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: love against duty, from the wounded side.

chapters.title: The Original's Last Night
chapters.summary: Dominic replays the murder's final hours and realizes the killer was the envoy's predecessor, acting on fleet consensus—not malice, but maintenance. She understands she was decanted to be a better liar. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: horror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax: during the loop's final cycle, Dominic and Rafael hijack Vector's array and transmit the full case—the fabricated loop, the murder, the truth—to both fleets simultaneously, betting shared knowledge prevents war. The envoy moves to stop them; the colony's remaining residents shield the antenna. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: terror, then terrible calm.

chapters.title: Vector, Remembered
chapters.summary: Resolution: the fleets hold fire, stunned into negotiation by mutual exposure. Dominic, stripped of rank and facing exile, chooses to stay at Vector with Rafael, renaming the colony's archive for her original. The last transmission loop ends; something honest begins. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, identity claimed rather than inherited.
